concerns.text: T014 declares '**Dependency**: T010 (or fallback T010a) and T011', but T011 (regulatory BED fetch) appears nowhere in the task list — not as a pending task, not as a checked task. The revision note claims T011 is 'preserved as checked', yet no checked T011 entry exists in this document. The regulatory BED is a hard producer input for T014; without a task (or a visible checked entry with its artifact path) the consumer-before-producer chain is broken and T014 is unexecutable as ordered.

T018 declares '**Dependency**: T014, T010b' and requires reference-genome context via pyfaidx, but T010b (reference genome fetch) has no task entry in this list — same missing-producer problem as T011. The revision note names T010b as 'preserved as checked' but the document contains no such entry, so the reference genome required by every scoring task has no visible producer.

T024 consumes the `is_gwas_lead` labels produced by T027 and the ΔScore distributions produced by T021, but states no dependency clause at all. The 'Execution order' line at the bottom places T027 before T024, but the task itself carries no dependency, so a scheduler honoring per-task dependencies could run T024 before its GWAS-label producer. Add '**Dependency**: T021, T027' to T024.

T008 is tagged [P] (parallel-safe) yet declares '**Dependency**: T007' and re-runs the full workflow whose report (T007) it must follow. A task with an explicit ordering dependency is not parallel-safe; either drop the [P] tag or remove the dependency. Same tension is weaker for T007 (depends on T006v) — both [P] tags on dependent tasks should be reconciled.

T013b (GC-matched controls, US1) is placed in Phase 2 after the US2 scoring tasks T018/T021, despite being a US1 data-ingestion deliverable and depending only on T014. This breaks the user-story grouping principle: US1's independently-shippable unit (filtered SNPs + control set + source log) cannot be tested end-to-end until Phase 2. Move T013b adjacent to T014 in Phase 1.
